Order 
The appellants have filed an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, read with Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act (IA No. 702 of 2017) seeking condonation of the delay in filing the appeal.
2. As per the office note, there is a delay of 90 days in filing the instant appeal.
3. Considering the reasons assigned in the application, the same is allowed, and the delay in filing the appeal is hereby condoned.

4. Heard on admission.
5.

The present miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellants- claimants under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, challenging the Award dated 24.10.2016 passed by the Third Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Shivpuri (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal")
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4534 2 MA-169-2017 in Claim Case No. 400141 of 2014, whereby the Claims Tribunal rejected the claim filed by the claimants, holding that they were not entitled to receive any compensation on the ground that the claimants failed to prove that the accident was caused by the driver of truck No. MP 06 HC 0490, namely, Manoj Jatav (herein respondent No.1).

1 6.
It is contended on behalf of the appellants that the accident occurred on 24.03.2013, and an FIR was lodged on the same day against the offending vehicle.
The statement of witnesses was recorded.
After the completion of the investigation, a charge sheet was filed against the driver of the offending vehicle-respondent No.1.
According to the appellants, this prima facie proves that the accident occurred.

The Claims Tribunal, however, committed a legal error by not considering the evidence of the appellants' witnesses and dismissing the claim merely on the ground that the truck number was not mentioned in the FIR.
The Claims Tribunal erred in rejecting the evidence of witnesses, Kamar Singh and Brakhbhan, and wrongly dismissed their claim.

7. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the respondent No.3 opposes the appellants'
contentions and supports the impugned Award, praying for dismissal of this miscellaneous appeal.
8.
Heard learned counsel for both parties.

9. Upon perusal of the record of the Claims Tribunal, it was found that Brakhbhan (AW-2) stated in his cross-examination that he knew the deceased, Purushottam, and was informed about the accident by Ghanshyam, a resident of the village.
Brakhbhan further stated that he did not report the incident immediately but went to Sheopur and returned after a day.
He did NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4534 3 MA-169-2017 not report the incident to the police station, which was nearby.
His failure to immediately report the accident to the police raises doubts about his credibility as a witness.
Further, Kamar Singh, the other eyewitness, stated in the FIR (Ex.P-1) that he was with Purushottam on the motorcycle and witnessed the accident.
However, his statement differed from the version of Brakhbhan.
While Kamar Singh's statement mentioned that the truck hit Purushottam as he was walking towards him, Brakhbhan's statement mentioned that Purushottam was hit while standing.
This inconsistency further casts doubt on the reliability of their testimonies.
Moreover, the FIR (Ex.P-1) did not mention the truck's number, which is a critical piece of evidence.
The appellants did not submit certified copies of statements under Section 161 of CrPC of the witnesses, which could have supported the claimants' case.
Also, there was no evidence of the investigating officer, which could have clarified whether the vehicle involved in the accident was the same truck referred to in the charge sheet.
The claimants failed to prove that the offending truck was involved in the accident.
The truck's number was not mentioned in the FIR, and the statements of witnesses did not align with details in the FIR.

Based on the above analysis, the Claims Tribunal concluded that the appellants had not been able to prove that respondent No.1, while in the employment of respondent No.2, had driven the offending truck rashly and negligently, causing the death of Purushottam.
It is found that the Claims Tribunal's findings are based on an analysis of the evidence on record, and the appellants have not been able to prove the material facts of the case.

The inconsistencies in testimonies of the witnesses, the lack of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:4534 4 MA-169-2017 important documentary evidence, and the failure to establish that the truck involved was the same vehicle named in the charge sheet.
10.
For the reasons stated above, the miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellants-claimants is hereby dismissed being devoid of merits.
No order as to costs.
